title: Carbon economics as a framework for interpreting responses to climate change: a commentary on ‘Differentiation for drought strategy but conserved plasticity to heat and drought in locally adapted populations of Arabidopsis thaliana’
content: Future ecosystem productivity and carbon storage will depend not only on changes in species composition, but also on how individual plants respond to environmental change. In this issue of the Annals of Botany, Buysse et al. (2026) show that locally adapted populations of Arabidopsis thaliana converge toward similar drought responses under simulated future climates. These findings raise broader questions about how climate change will influence plant adaptation and ecosystem function. Carbon economics provides a framework for addressing these questions by describing how plants acquire, allocate and retain resources for growth, survival and reproduction. Through this lens, climate change may alter ecosystem carbon storage not only by changing species composition, but also by reshaping the carbon-economic strategies plants deploy.
